messages:
Tasha: Heads up — after the 1766 runtime rollout a subset of canary traffic is showing p99 tail jumps (~3x). Support ticket #INC-12345. Anyone on-call to triage?
Jamal: noted. I see the alert in grafana — p95 is ok, p99 spikes on long-request cohorts only. linking dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/runtime/p95-p99
Anna: can you confirm this is the canary group only? sound like a kernel/assembly change.
Tasha: yes, only canary and small fraction of prod routed to canary (10%). 1.8% of requests hitting p99 > 800ms up from ~250ms.
Mike: grabbing logs. Initial look: increased number of KV cache misses and a lot of slow open/close on the executor loop. suspect the new scheduler patch.
Sara: any repro steps? good to have curl snippet to hit long seqs.
Tasha: repro snippet I used: ```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"<1000 token prompt>"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" --repeat 30```
Tasha: when I run locally against canary endpoint p99 jumps, against baseline it stays low.
Jamal: putting canary to 0% while we triage. oncall, can you confirm rollout pause executed?
deploy-bot: Rollout pause command accepted. Canary traffic set to 0% for release/1766 by deploy-bot.
oncall: confirmed pause executed. No new canary traffic.
Anna: capture flamegraphs from canary pods and baseline pods for same trace ids. metric ids: trace:tr-9a1b. Also look at thread contention metrics: runtime.thread_lock_wait_ms.
Mike: gathered profiles. attaching quick diff: canary shows 4x time in scheduler::choose_kernel and increased lock hold in kvcache::put.
Sara: that points at kernel-selector change in 1766. Did we land the microbatch scheduler tweak?
Jamal: yes, changeset 1766 included kernel-selector heuristics + an optimization that changed eviction timing in KV cache.
Tasha: support report shows API errors are low — not an increase in 5xx. This is pure tail latency. Customers complaining about chat timeouts.
Anna: temporary mitigation ideas: 1) revert kernel-selector tweak; 2) bump KV cache size or reduce eviction aggressiveness via runtime config; 3) route high-seq-length traffic to baseline model variant.
Mike: quick hotfix we can try: increase kv_cache_capacity to 2x on canary nodes, restart runtime processes, measure. low-risk config change.
Jamal: I'm running kv cache bump on canary group now, will watch p99.
Tasha: also please enable detailed request tracing for the cohort. add tag cohort=long-seq.
deploy-bot: Config change applied to canary nodes: runtime.kv_cache_capacity=2x by deploy-bot (change-id ch-789).
Mike: initial numbers — p99 reduced by ~30% after cache bump but still higher than baseline.
Sara: suggests root cause is combined: kernel-selector change increases scheduler time per request, cache evictions exacerbate tail for long sequences. Need bisect.
Jamal: plan: 1) revert kernel-selector tweak in a canary build and test; 2) if revert fixes, roll rollback for full release; 3) otherwise bisect other changes in 1766.
Tasha: agree. Jamal, can you produce a rollback build and coordinate smoke tests? include the long-seq curl loop.
Jamal: building rollback image now (1766-rollback-1). ETA ~12 mins. I'll post smoke results.
Mike: adding a short-term traffic policy to route high-token sequences to baseline until root cause is confirmed. config: route_rule(token_length>512)->baseline.
Anna: also add a metric alert for unusual kvcache miss ratio spikes so we don't miss this next time.
Tasha: customer comms: support will inform affected customers that we paused canary and are investigating, ETA 1h.
Sara: on the bisect: if rollback fixes, we'll create a follow-up PR to reintroduce kernel-selector change with tests for thread_lock_wait_ms.
Jamal: rollback build smoke tests: 1) curl loop x30 against canary endpoints with rollback image; 2) compare p99 vs baseline. Running now...
(5m) Jamal: smoke done. p99 on rollback canary matches baseline within 5%. Seems like kernel-selector tweak is the smoking gun. :mag_right:
Tasha: great — proceed to roll forward the rollback (i.e., deploy previous kernel behavior) and schedule a proper bisect + perf test before re-landing.
deploy-bot: Rollout started: deploying image rwd-runtime:1765 to canary by deploy-bot.
oncall: monitoring cluster during rollout.
Mike: post-rollback graphs look stable. p99 back to baseline for the cohort.
Tasha: follow-ups: - write a regression test that runs long-sequence load on PRs changing scheduler/kernel selection - add kvcache miss ratio alert - update runbook to include quick kv_cache bump steps and traffic routing policy snippets - create postmortem once customer impact quantified
Sara: I'll draft the runbook PR. Jamal, please include the exact git diff and the kernel-selector change lines for the postmortem.
Jamal: will do. posting final notes to #incidents and tagging support.
Tasha: thanks all — great triage. Closing thread once postmortem link added. :thumbsup:
